notes.text: lamb to the ruler. As a tribute, and following the formalities of the period, the Moabite refugees sent a lamb to the ruler in Judah. This recalls 2 Kgs. 3:4, which describes Mesha, king of Moab, giving a tribute to the king of Judah of one hundred thousand lambs and one hundred thousand rams with their wool.

notes.text: Heshbon, Sibmah, Jazer, Elealeh, and Kir-haresh. These are principal Moabite cities connected with the wine industry and are mentioned here to indicate the industry's breadth. Isaiah also recounts that "her
branches are stretched out, they are gone over the sea," which indicates that Moab's wine export business was regionally and perhaps even internationally known
